### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a53fc9feac04d44f40fffc62f93d04433de1227`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a53fc9feac04d44f40fffc62f93d04433de1227` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `169a5cc19f9a5bd6c6750044994fc6dbd78d5e23` — the merge of head `89c379ba6e21e5650ad7e8900a5fdc361942d8c9` into base `9a53fc9feac04d44f40fffc62f93d04433de1227`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 169a5cc19f9a5bd6c6750044994fc6dbd78d5e23 && git checkout 169a5cc19f9a5bd6c6750044994fc6dbd78d5e23
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9a53fc9feac04d44f40fffc62f93d04433de1227 89c379ba6e21e5650ad7e8900a5fdc361942d8c9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9a53fc9feac04d44f40fffc62f93d04433de1227 && git merge --no-ff 89c379ba6e21e5650ad7e8900a5fdc361942d8c9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a53fc9feac04d44f40fffc62f93d04433de1227
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9a53fc9feac04d44f40fffc62f93d04433de1227` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3aa77b9a7f45449166602cfaa2ea550eaf40fad5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/objects/system-file.object.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/attachments-permission-matrix.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx, .changeset/sys-file-uploader-is-its-creator.md + packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts

Face: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `!`. Net diff read against merge-base `232d3bb5ef` (7 files, +280/-10); all cited code read on `origin/main` at `9a53fc9fea`. Every non-skipped check-run on the head is `success`, the ten required contexts included (Lint UI, Type Check UI and Build & E2E UI skipped by path filter). Precedent #29868 (merged `6f35b746f0`) read.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Placement.** The stamp sits inside the existing `beforeInsert` handler of `installSysFileStorageOwnedColumnsGuard`, after the `isSystem` return and the data-shape guard, before the lifecycle-column strip. On `main`, `sys_file` has exactly one registration naming `object: 'sys_file'` (installed once in `storage-service-plugin.ts` at `kernel:ready`); the only other `beforeInsert` registrations in service-storage target `sys_attachment` or are wildcard by `packageId`. The PR adds no registration, so `sys_file` keeps one. The unit test pins the registration list as `[['beforeInsert', 'sys_file']]`. Holds.
- **Match to the attachment hook.** Same three legs as `attachment-access-hooks.ts`'s create hook and `comment-access-hooks.ts`'s: `isSystem` keeps the supplied value; a non-system session records `session.userId` over whatever the create carried; a session whose `userId` is not a non-empty string is refused 403 with the same catalog code the two siblings refuse theirs with. The bare-kernel carve-out (no session at all keeps the supplied value) is the siblings' `if (!ctx?.session) return`, expressed here as `if (ctx?.session) recordUploader(...)`. Holds.
- **The deliberate difference.** Right. The lifecycle-column strip was already judged "every write whose context is not `isSystem`, a context-less one included" on `main`, and that is the update strip's rule too; the uploader rule has nobody to record on a context-less call, so it keeps what was supplied, as the siblings do. Narrowing the uploader rule did not have to widen the strip, and the PR does not. The unit test pins both halves on one context-less call (value kept, `status` reset to `pending`, `key` dropped).
- **Silence.** The overwrite is silent, as `uploaded_by` and `author_id` are. The engine's insert-side readonly strip returns a null subject for any `sys_` object (`staticReadonlyInsertSubject`), so no `droppedFields` entry is produced on this create and nothing is reported. The dev's supporting claim is overstated, though: the hook contract does carry a member a hook can speak to the requester through, `ctx.notice` (the write's `onNotice` listener, bound on every insert dispatch). It carries a free-text save notice, not a dropped-field report, and neither sibling stamp uses it, so silence stays the right reading of the ruling ("as the attachment and comment create hooks stamp"). The sentence in the module docblock and PR body saying the contract declares no such member should be corrected (should-fix, below).
- **Unchanged surfaces.** The upload doors write through `StorageMetadataStore.createFile` under `systemInsertOptionsFor` (`isSystem: true`), which the hook returns on first; the diff touches none of presign, chunked or complete, and the integration test pins both doors still recording the uploading user. The update path is untouched: `owner_id` is `readonly: true` on `main` and the engine's update strip handles it; the integration test pins an update leaving the create's uploader and a system update changing it. `git grep` on `main` finds one data-API writer of `sys_file` outside tests, that same store under the system context, so no caller in `packages/` or `ui/` changes.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-storage` with `!` and a BREAKING banner: correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no key, value or type an author writes moves), and under the level rule a `none` kind takes `patch` whatever the breakage, keeping its banner and ADR-0087 disposition.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: correct arm. A runtime accept set narrows (a supplied `owner_id` no longer lands on a non-system create; a no-user create is refused); nothing widens.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: correct. No stored row is read, rewritten or dropped; no spec key, export or stored shape moves; the remedy for a writer that needs a different uploader recorded is a system-context write, which no ledger entry can derive. The changeset closes the other categories on facts, as the marker form asks.
- The BREAKING banner names who moves (a client creating `sys_file` through the data API; a server-side caller creating with no signed-in user) and the fix for each (the row is recorded under the caller; write from a system context, or run as the system principal or name the user acted for). The console and upload doors are named as needing nothing. `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green on the head. Holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The order's update-time transfer assumption.** The dev is right and A is the answer. Since #29868, `sys_file.owner_id` is `readonly: true`, so the engine's update strip drops a non-system caller's value, the holder of the ownership-transfer grant included (pinned on `main` by the dogfood block's PATCH case: 200 with `owner_id` in `droppedFields`, stored value unchanged; the docs page says so in words). An update-time transfer under `allowTransfer` is not a path that exists on `main`, and this ruling's provenance is #29868's rule that authorship is read-only after creation. Nothing in the PR changes; the seat corrects its own order wording.
- **The dev's private lead (2).** Read at the plumbing, `buildSession` copies `userId`, `tenantId`, `positions`, `accessToken`, `isSystem`, `actor` and three opt-out flags, then returns `undefined` when every one is `undefined`; `principalKind` is not copied. So a context carrying only `principalKind` would indeed read as context-less to every sibling carve-out. But no guest door can produce that shape: the one producer of `principalKind` on `main` is `assembleExecutionContextOrGuest`, whose guest envelope always carries `positions: ['guest']` (emitted, since defined), so `buildSession` yields a session with no `userId`, and the create is refused, not admitted. No non-test source constructs `principalKind` by hand (every other hit is a comment). An agent envelope keeps `userId` as the human. Verdict: not a must-measure follow-up; the measurement is done by reading. The carve-out's safety is keyed on the guest envelope carrying a session-bearing field rather than on `principalKind`, which is worth one pin in the plumbing's own test (should-fix follow-up, not in this PR).
- **The Verification block.** The body says the dogfood battery is NOT MEASURED on this head and points to the dev report; the battery has since run green at the head (417 files / 3464 tests). A reading cited is a count plus the tree it was taken against, and the body is the record a later reader greps, so the seat corrects that block to carry the reading before landing. Should-fix, not blocking: the body states a conservative truth as of writing, not a false one, and the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is independent green evidence.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the published surface on `main` and the ruling: the narrowing makes a provenance rule real at the one door it was missing from (a `sys_file` created through the data API), aligned with the two sibling stamps and the read-only-after-creation rule of #29868. Attempts to break it:

- **`owner_id` null or empty on a create.** The stamp assigns `session.userId` unconditionally after the no-user check, so a null, empty or absent value is overwritten the same as another user's id; the unit test pins the absent case. Holds.
- **Bulk create.** Both batch doors reach the engine's `insert`/`insertMany`, whose `beforeInsert` runs once per row with that row as `input.data` (pinned on `main` by the engine's insert-many test), so the guard's early return on an array input is never the path a batch takes. The integration test pins a two-row batch recording the caller on each row. Holds.
- **Impersonating or on-behalf-of caller.** Impersonation mints a session for the target user, so `userId` is the impersonated user and the row records them, as `uploaded_by` and `author_id` would. An agent acting on behalf of a human keeps `userId` as the human, with the client on `provenance.performedBy`; the row records the human, as the siblings do. Consistent with the ruling; no finding.
- **Guest or service-principal caller.** A guest envelope and a service-principal context (`actor` only) both yield a session with no `userId` and are refused; the integration test pins the service-principal case writing no row. Fail-closed. Holds.
- **Docs page claims.** Each claim on `attachments-access.mdx` matches the code: data-API create records the signed-in user; no-user create refused 403 `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`; update drops a non-system caller's value and reports it. The closing sentence "Only a system-context write records a different uploader" omits the context-less bare-kernel case the changeset names; the page addresses the platform doors, where no such call exists, so no change is required (note only).
- **§6 rule-level check.** Title, body, changeset, commit messages, docs page and every test name state the hardening rule and its controls, none an attack; the module docblock likewise. No breach.

Findings:
- **Should-fix (this PR, comment-only):** the sentence "the hook contract declares no member through which a hook reports one" in the `sys-file-storage-owned-columns.ts` docblock and the PR body. The contract carries `ctx.notice`; what it lacks is a dropped-field report, and the sibling stamps use no notice either. Say that instead.
- **Should-fix (PR body, before landing):** replace the NOT MEASURED dogfood line with the reading at the head.
- **Should-fix (follow-up, not this PR):** a pin that `buildSession` of a guest envelope is defined, so the context-less carve-out never admits an anonymous request.
- **Must-fix:** none.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-v`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `89c379ba6e21e5650ad7e8900a5fdc361942d8c9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.ts + packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts

Delta review: the prior PASS stands at `3aa77b9a7f`; this record judges `git diff 3aa77b9a7f..89c379ba6e`, the rewritten PR body and the new head's check-runs. The delta is one commit, comment-only, in the guard's module docblock (5 insertions, 4 deletions, no code line moved). Face unchanged: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `!`.

### ① Derived judgments

- The one hunk rewrites the "silence" paragraph of the docblock: it now says the engine reports a dropped field only for the strips it runs itself and runs none on a `sys_` object's create, that the hook contract carries no dropped-field report, that its caller-facing member `ctx.notice` is a free-text save notice, and that neither sibling stamp uses it. Each clause matches the contract on `main` (`HookContext.notice`, a `HookNoticeSetter` bound at every insert/update dispatch and answered as the write's `notice`; no `droppedFields` member on the context) and the two sibling hooks (no `notice` call in either create stamp). The prior should-fix 1 is applied as asked.
- No behaviour moves: the handler, `recordUploader`, `refuseNoUploader`, the strip and the registration are byte-identical to the reviewed head. The reviewed verdicts on placement, sibling match, the deliberate difference and the unchanged surfaces carry over.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still correct: `patch` on `@objectstack/service-storage` with `!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; the changeset is untouched by the delta.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body.** The same sentence is corrected in the body ("the hook contract carries no dropped-field report: its one caller-facing member, `ctx.notice`, is a free-text save notice"), so body and docblock agree with each other and with the contract.
- **Verification reading.** The body now carries the dogfood battery as a count plus the tree it was taken against (on `3aa77b9a7f` under the verify lock: command-exit 0, Test Files 417 passed and 3 skipped of 420, Tests 3464 passed and 28 skipped of 3492), and states that `89c379ba6e` adds one comment-only commit on which the guard tests (2 files, 38 tests) and the 49 derived gate families for the changed file were re-read green. A comment-only delta needs no battery re-run; the body says which tree each reading is from. Prior should-fix 2 is applied.
- **Check-runs on the new head.** All ten required contexts are green: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI and Live E2E UI `success`; Lint UI, Type Check UI and Build & E2E UI `skipped` by path filter. Dogfood Regression Gate `success`. Two advisory runs (Check Changeset, PR-body guards) show a second `in_progress` instance started after the body edit; their first instances on this same head completed `success`, and neither is in the required set.
- **Still open, not for this PR:** the follow-up pin that `buildSession` of a guest envelope is defined (prior should-fix 3).

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is unchanged from the reviewed head and holds for the same reasons. §6 check on the delta: the new docblock paragraph, the commit message ("the sys_file guard's docblock names ctx.notice as a save notice, not a dropped-field report") and the rewritten body sentences state the rule and the contract, nothing of an attack; no breach. The docblock's "one caller-facing member" is accurate for what a hook can say to the requester (`api` is data access, `notice` the only answer-bound member). No finding; no must-fix.

ACCEPT · head `89c379ba6e21e5650ad7e8900a5fdc361942d8c9` · 2026-11-04T20:33Z

- **Shape:** 7 files, +281/−10. Not governed. Under 3000. Patch for service-storage, with `!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- **Rule held** (security-channel ruling of 2026-11-04, batch 4 item 7, under #29868): a stored file's uploader is the user who created it, the same rule as an attachment's and a comment's author.

  - System context and the upload doors are unchanged.

The delta record on this head is comment 6641419007: `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, `Head-sha` equals this head, VERDICT PASS, no must-fix. Two of the review's should-fixes are applied (the docblock sentence and the Verification reading).

- **Gates (dev):** 49 derived families run, 0 NOT MEASURED. Guard tests: 38 passed. Full dogfood battery at the code head: 417 files, 3464 tests. Ablation: red, then restored.
- **Seat correction:** the dispatch order assumed an update-time transfer of this column under the transfer grant. There is no such path: #29868 made the column read-only. The order's wording was wrong; the PR is unchanged.
